catalogMeta.label: Build a Paragraph (open build)
catalogMeta.description: Open build, on the live tutor: tap sentence cards into a paragraph in order: the topic sentence first, two or more facts that belong (any order), the closing last, leaving out the two facts about a different topic. Many paragraphs pass. Checked in code from the cards' roles. Organization only; the writing modes judge no sentence. Beta = informational + 0.1.

cards.text: Sea turtles are reptiles that swim in the ocean.
They have hard shells to protect their bodies.
Their large flippers help them glide through water.
Mother turtles lay their eggs in sandy nests.
They can hold their breath for several hours.
Blue whales are the largest animals on Earth.
Dolphins jump high out of the salty water.
Now you know all about sea turtles.
Octopuses are clever sea animals with eight arms.
They can squirt dark ink to hide quickly.
Their soft bodies can squeeze into tiny holes.
They change skin colors to blend with rocks.
Suction cups line the underside of each arm.
Jellyfish do not have brains or hearts.
Crabs walk sideways across the ocean floor.
These facts show how octopuses are special.
Clownfish are bright fish that live in warm reefs.
They have vivid orange and white stripes.
A slimy coat protects them from stinging anemones.
They eat tiny ocean plants and drifting food.
Clownfish stay close to their safe sea home.
Great white sharks have rows of sharp teeth.
Sea otters float on their backs to rest.
That is how clownfish live in the sea.
